:::{#exm-decidable}
#### Decidable problems from P and NP

The palindromes are [decidable](#def-decidable),
because the machine of
[the palindrome example](models-of-computation.qmd#exm-palindromes-linear-time)
[decides](models-of-computation.qmd#def-tm-computes) them.
[INDSET](p-and-np.qmd#def-indset) is decidable too,
even though no [polynomial-time](p-and-np.qmd#def-running-time) algorithm for it is known.
It is in [NP](p-and-np.qmd#def-class-np),
whose definition gives a verifier and a certificate length $q(\strlen{x})$.
A machine can run the verifier on each of the $2^{q(\strlen{x})}$ possible certificates in turn,
and accept if any certificate passes.
That search takes exponential time,
but it always [halts](models-of-computation.qmd#def-turing-machine).
Decidability asks only whether a machine that always halts exists,
not how long it takes.

:::
